primary_meaning: The northern kingdom of Israel (the ten tribes), often as a figure of apostate or idolatrous Israel
primary_basis: Genesis 48:8–20 (rise of the tribe as leading house of Joseph)

alternatives.meaning: Fruitfulness / double fruitfulness (etymological symbol drawn from the name)
basis: Genesis 49:22 (Joseph as fruitful bough, applied to Ephraim)

alternatives.meaning: Divine election / preference of the younger over the older (type of sovereign grace)
The ‘fullness of the nations’ / Gentile inclusion or ‘lost tribes’ identity (two-house or British-Israel readings of melo ha-goyim)
The Church itself (allegorical transfer of northern-Israel imagery)
basis: Hosea applied typologically to the Church
occasional patristic or later spiritualizing readings

notes: Standard Christian biblical interpretation and preaching treat ‘Ephraim’ as the conventional prophetic designation for the northern kingdom/Israel, especially in Hosea and related prophets; the other senses appear but are secondary or specialized.
